Additionally, Regorafenib is classified as a cytochrome P450 2c9 inhibitor, and Efavirenz, a known inhibitor of Cyp2b6, is included in this class. This implies that Regorafenib may exert its effects on Cyp2b6 through a shared mechanism of inhibition, possibly via interaction with the same or related enzymes. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential role for Regorafenib in modulating Cyp2b6 activity, likely through the inhibition of P450 enzymes, which in turn affects the metabolism of substrates that interact with Cyp2b6. The evidence supports a plausible link between Regorafenib and Cyp2b6, mediated through the cytochrome P450 pathway, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
